item.title: Elevators, toasters, and the birth of Java
item.content:encoded: Ryan sits down with James Gosling, creator of Java at Sun Microsystems, to talk about the early networking friction that drove the need for interconnectedness, the stringent reliability requirements of consumer electronics companies that inspired the Java virtual machine, and the evolution of garbage collectors that allow Java to handle large-scale concurrent memory management.

item.title: Rumors of the SaaS demise are greatly exaggerated
item.content:encoded: Recorded on the floor of LDX3, Ryan chats with Nivia Henry, an engineering leader most recently at Netflix, about the reality of the supposed SaaS apocalypse, the complex calculus of the modern build-versus-buy decision in the era of AI, and the critical importance of understanding system architectures to manage long-term infrastructure costs.

The data says they’re already swapping models in and out, but the trap they’re concerned about is the layer on top of the model.

item.title: Don't forget about the UI for AI
